fixed_statement:
Let \(m\ge1\), and let \(w_1,\ldots,w_m\ge0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i=1\).
For \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), write \(w(B)=\sum_{i\in B}w_i\).
At least \(2^{m-1}\) subsets \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) satisfy
\[
w(B)\ge1/2.
\]
fixed_proof:
Pair every subset \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with its complement \(B^c\). These pairs partition the \(2^m\) subsets into \(2^{m-1}\) unordered pairs. Since
\[
w(B)+w(B^c)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i=1,
\]
at least one of \(B\) and \(B^c\) has weight at least \(1/2\).
